why: callToolHandler -> KnowledgeGraphManager.createEntities -> Neo4jStorageProvider.createEntities builds the CREATE (e:Entity {...}) query entirely from named Cypher parameters ($id,$name,$entityType,$observations,...); entity.name/entityType/observations are only ever bound as parameter values, never spliced into the query text.

Neo4jStorageProvider.createRelations MATCHes endpoints by {name:$fromName}/{name:$toName} and CREATEs the relation with all fields ($id,$relationType,$strength,...) as bound parameters; no string concatenation of caller data into Cypher text.

addObservations handler only writes obs.entityName/contents to stderr debug logs (not a structured/parsed log) and to KnowledgeGraphManager.addObservations, which reaches Neo4jStorageProvider.addObservations; every MATCH/CREATE/SET there uses $name/$id/$observations parameters, so entityName and contents never enter Cypher syntax.

Neo4jStorageProvider.deleteEntities runs `MATCH (e:Entity) WHERE e.name IN $names DETACH DELETE e` with entityNames bound as the $names list parameter; no injection surface, and this is the tool's advertised destructive purpose.

deletions[].entityName/observations flow into Neo4jStorageProvider.deleteObservations, which only uses them as $name parameters and via JS array .filter()/.includes() for the observation-content diff; nothing is concatenated into a query string.

Neo4jStorageProvider.deleteRelations runs `MATCH (from...)-[r:RELATES_TO]->(to...) WHERE r.relationType = $relationType DELETE r` with relation.from/to/relationType bound as parameters ($fromName,$toName,$relationType).

callToolHandler builds an `options` object from args.reference_time/args.decay_factor, but KnowledgeGraphManager.getDecayedGraph() (src/KnowledgeGraphManager.ts:1160) takes zero parameters and just calls storageProvider.getDecayedGraph() with no arguments, so any options the caller supplies are silently dropped before reaching Neo4jStorageProvider.getDecayedGraph, which only queries validTo IS NULL with no user-controlled parameters at all.

args.entity_name is used only via openNodes([name]) and storageProvider.getEntityEmbedding(name)/getEntity(name), both of which bind the name as the Cypher $name parameter in a `MATCH (e:Entity {name:$name})` pattern; read-only lookup, no injection surface.
Neo4jStorageProvider.getEntityHistory runs `MATCH (e:Entity {name:$name}) RETURN e ORDER BY e.validFrom ASC` with entityName bound as $name; purely a parameterized read.

args.timestamp is passed straight through to Neo4jStorageProvider.getGraphAtTime, which binds it as the $timestamp parameter in `WHERE e.validFrom <= $timestamp AND (e.validTo IS NULL OR e.validTo > $timestamp)`; a non-numeric value just fails the comparison, no injection or path/command surface.
args.from/args.to/args.relationType are bound as $fromName/$toName/$relationType in a parameterized MATCH in Neo4jStorageProvider.getRelation; read-only, no injection surface.
Neo4jStorageProvider.getRelationHistory binds from/to/relationType as parameters in a MATCH...ORDER BY query; purely parameterized read, no sink for injection.
names[] is bound as the $names list parameter in `MATCH (e:Entity) WHERE e.name IN $names` (Neo4jStorageProvider.openNodes); no string concatenation into Cypher text.
read_graph takes no arguments; handleReadGraph calls knowledgeGraphManager.readGraph() which is an alias for loadGraph()/storageProvider.loadGraph() with zero caller-controlled input.

args.relation's from/to/relationType/strength/confidence/metadata are all bound as named parameters ($fromName,$toName,$relationType,$strength,...) across the MATCH/SET/CREATE steps in Neo4jStorageProvider.updateRelation; metadata is JSON.stringify'd before being passed as a parameter value, not interpolated into query text.

sink: caller string is embedded verbatim (only wrapped with `(?i).*` / `.*`) into a regex string, bound as the Cypher $query parameter, and evaluated server-side via `e.name =~ $query OR e.entityType =~ $query OR e.observations =~ $query` (line 481) against every Entity node's name/entityType/observations
why: Traced callToolHandler.ts:83-91 (`knowledgeGraphManager.searchNodes(args.query)`) -> KnowledgeGraphManager.searchNodes (delegates straight to storageProvider since a Neo4j StorageProvider is present) -> Neo4jStorageProvider.searchNodes, which builds the regex string by naive template interpolation and runs it through Neo4j's `=~` operator, which uses Java's backtracking regex engine. listToolsHandler.ts declares `query` as an opaque free-text string ('match against entity names, types, and observation content'), giving no indication to the caller that it is regex syntax, and there is no length cap, metacharacter escaping, or execution timeout anywhere on this path. An adversarial value such as query=`(a+)+$` yields the compiled pattern `(?i).*(a+)+$.*`, which triggers catastrophic backtracking against long observation/entityType strings already stored in the graph (attacker can also first store such a string via add_observations), tying up the Neo4j query thread and, by extension, the MCP server's single request-processing path. Checked node_modules/neo4j-driver 5.28.1: session.run()/executeQuery() only serializes and transmits parameters over Bolt, performing no regex validation or sanitization; the regex is actually evaluated inside the external Neo4j DBMS process, which is not a vendored dependency of this repo.
contract: The search query to match against entity names, types, and observation content

why: callToolHandler.ts case 'semantic_search' calls knowledgeGraphManager.search(String(args.query), {...}), which (KnowledgeGraphManager.ts:924-939) calls storageProvider.semanticSearch(query,{queryVector,...}) when an embedding service exists, else falls back directly to storageProvider.searchNodes(query). Inside Neo4jStorageProvider.semanticSearch itself, if options.queryVector is still unset after attempting to generate it (embeddingService missing, e.g. no OPENAI_API_KEY configured, or generateEmbedding throwing), it falls through to `this.searchNodes(query, {...options, limit: textSearchLimit})` at line 2212 -- the exact same vulnerable regex-construction sink as search_nodes. This is Tier B rather than A because it requires the deployment-specific condition that no working embedding service is configured/available, which cannot be confirmed to be present or absent from static reading alone; the underlying mechanism when it does fire is identical to the search_nodes finding.
